## At a glance

- **Driven by.** [[Sable]], the drowned bell-ringer of Vessen, and the coming Long Ebb.
- **Stands at.** The Party has the [[Harbormaster's Ledger of Vessen]] and has read its last entry. The bell has stopped ringing.
- **If nobody acts.** On 1 Hollowdark, the Long Ebb opens [[The Drowned Chapel]] to the Reedrunners and the Council alike.
- **Levers.** The names of the drowned, the ledger, and the [[Ebb Lantern]].

## Play

- **Shows up as.** The bell at night, a drowned man on dry boards, silt lines too high for a storm, and villagers who change the subject.
- **Next development.** The Party must decide whom to tell. If the ledger is spoken aloud in [[Reedholt]], [[Sable]] will rest. If it is sold, the bell will ring again.
- **Levers.** [[Nib Ashwater]] holds the list of the drowned. [[Hobb Tarrow]] holds a family secret. [[Odalys Ferro]] can bring the church's silence into it.
- **Resolves when.** The truth of [[The Drowning of Vessen]] is spoken in public, or the ledger is destroyed.

## Depth

### Origin

The Thread began on 6 Blackwater 271 CY. It has lain still for 141 years, and woke when the sluice began to fail and the sea drew out early.

### Hidden truths

- The bell rings because the water that drowned Vessen is not fully gone. It moves under the mud, and it rings the bell. The Party can learn this by putting a hand on the bell in the loft.
- Sable is not alone. Other Vessen dead lie in the flats, and they wait for her signal. The Party can learn this by watching how the Mire Drowner creatures behave when she speaks.

### Possible endings

- The Party speaks the names aloud in [[Reedholt]] and the ledger goes to the moot. Sable rests and the bell stops ringing.
- The Party gives the ledger to [[Ilse Corran]] and the Harbor Council falls, and the bell rings again at every tide.
- The Party gives the ledger to [[Hobb Tarrow]] and the Council hides it. Vessen's truth is lost, and the drowned remain.
